purpose: Independent practice of D2.2 — testing predictions in different groups.
student_learning_goal: I can test a prediction in a new group.

header.student_learning_goal_banner: I can test a prediction in a new group.
header.character_watermark: Maybe Mae the Cat in the top-right corner with a clipboard. Small (~1.5in tall). References blueprint.recurring_characters.

parts.student_instructions: Look at our class data. Predict for ANOTHER class. Then look at the other class data. Was your prediction right?
parts.visual_layout: Top: our class data table (Pets — 12 dogs, 6 cats, 2 fish). Middle: a prediction line for the other class. Bottom: another class data (different counts) for comparison.

image_placeholders.description: A two-class comparison layout for a Grade 1 worksheet, B&W line art. Top: a small data table titled 'Our Class' with rows: dogs (12), cats (6), fish (2). Middle: a prediction line 'I predict for the OTHER class: ___'. Bottom: a second data table titled 'Ms. B's Class' with rows: dogs (8), cats (9), fish (3) for the child to read and compare.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS04_P1_CLASSES at Part 1: instructions ask the child to predict for and test against another class. Keywords name the visual elements (class, data) and activity (predict).

parts.answer_key: Any prediction. Comparison should note: in our class, dogs were greatest. In Ms. B's class, cats were greatest. So a 'dogs' prediction would be wrong; a 'cats' prediction would be right.

parts.student_instructions: Predict pet preferences at HOME and at SCHOOL. Then test (ask 2 people each).
parts.visual_layout: A 2-column table. Columns: 'HOME' and 'SCHOOL'. Each column has a prediction line and a result line.

image_placeholders.description: A 2-column comparison table for a Grade 1 worksheet, B&W line art. Columns labelled 'HOME' (left) and 'SCHOOL' (right), each ~3in × 3in. Each column has 2 rows: a 'My prediction: ___' line and a 'What I found: ___' line, with generous writing space.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS04_P2_TABLE at Part 2: instructions ask the child to predict and test in 2 settings. Keywords name the two groups.

parts.answer_key: Any predictions and results. Common: home prediction = 'dog' (predicted from family pets), school prediction = 'dog' or 'cat'. Results vary by household and class.

parts.student_instructions: Write WHY predictions can be different in different groups.
parts.visual_layout: A bordered writing box ~5in × 1.8in. Above: 'Predictions can be different because...'.

image_placeholders.description: A bordered writing box for a Grade 1 worksheet. ~5in × 1.8in with thin solid border. Empty inside. Above the box, the printed prompt 'Predictions can be different because...'. Faint guide-lines at the bottom for handwriting.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS04_P3_BOX at Part 3: instructions ask the child to explain why groups differ. Keywords name the prompt focus.

parts.answer_key: Any sensible reason. Common: 'different people like different things', 'each group has different favourites', 'groups can be small or big'.

early_finisher_prompt: If you finish, predict for a 3rd group. Test it.
teacher_notes: Lesson 4 consolidation artifact. Use Part 3 as the formative signal — children who articulate 'different groups have different preferences' have grasped D2.2.
